features.description: Token foundation + shared component layer (the missing primitives). Add to core.css the semantic color aliases (status-ok/attention/blocked/info/muted), a spacing scale (--space-1..8) and a type scale (--text-xs..2xl + leading + mono/sans families) — none of which exist today. Build the shared components per docs/dashboard-design-system.md §4: Button (.btn primary/secondary/ghost), CopyCommand (.copy-cmd: a command block + copy button with a visible 'Copied' success state AND a visible failure hint), Card (.card with status accents), StatTile + StatStrip, SectionHeader, Banner, Skeleton. Reuse the existing .status-badge/.panel/.empty-state. Provide matching render helpers in lib/ (e.g. lib/components.js) so pages compose primitives instead of hand-rolling markup.
steps: Add semantic color aliases + spacing scale + type scale tokens to core.css :root
Build the component CSS (Button, CopyCommand w/ copied+failed states, Card, StatTile, StatStrip, SectionHeader, Banner, Skeleton) in core.css or a components.css loaded by index.html
Add lib/components.js render helpers that emit those primitives (escaped), incl. a copy-command helper that wires the existing copy handler + feedback
Unit-test the render helpers (markup shape, escaping, copied/failed affordance present)
features.acceptance: The shared base stylesheet and token layer expose semantic color aliases + a spacing scale + a type scale, plus a shared component layer (button, copy-command, card, stat-tile/strip, section-header, banner, skeleton) with matching render helpers. The copy-command primitive emits a labelled copy control with a visible success state and a visible failure hint. Verified by component unit tests asserting each primitive's markup + the copy success/failure affordances (no page behavior changes here); the primitives then enter the real shell through the F003 Repair real-state→real-shell journey test.

features.description: Page skeleton + shell hardening. Add a renderPage() helper that lays out every tab as title → summary stat-strip → primary actions → content → provenance footer (docs/dashboard-design-system.md §3), so no page hand-rolls its root markup. Harden the shell: wrap pages in a <main> landmark, add a skip-to-content link, add a global :focus-visible ring token + rule, and reorder the nav to task priority (Needs Attention · Repair · Work · Health · Architecture · Tools & Setup · Preferences).
steps: Add renderPage()/page-skeleton CSS (.page/.page-header/.page-summary/.page-content/.page-footer)
index.html + core.js: wrap page container in <main>, add a skip-to-content link, add a global :focus-visible rule using a --focus-ring token
Reorder pageModules so the nav leads with Needs Attention then Repair

Journey assertion: boot the shell with producer state; assert the main landmark + skip link exist, nav order matches the new priority order, interactive controls are keyboard-focusable, and the focus-ring rule/token is present in CSS
features.acceptance: A shared renderPage() skeleton + a hardened shell (main landmark, skip-to-content link, a focus-ring token + global focus-visible rule, task-priority nav order) are in place. Verified by a real-state→real-shell journey assertion that boots the shell with producer-generated state and checks: the main landmark + skip link exist, the nav order matches the new priority order, interactive controls are keyboard-focusable, and the focus-ring rule/token is present in CSS. True visual focus-ring rendering is NOT asserted in jsdom — it is deferred to a later Playwright pass.

features.description: Migrate Repair as the worked example (the worst-scoring tab; today it has NO stylesheet, shows 173 items as a count with none listed, and its 'Repair automatically' button copies a command while the label implies execution). Rebuild Repair on the F001/F002 primitives: a StatStrip for the counts (lead with the actionable number), the missing per-item LIST grouped by safety class (auto-safe / human-required / blocked-external / info), CopyCommand actions whose visible labels start with 'Copy' and show copied/failed feedback, and proper empty/zero/error states. This stays a RENDER-LAYER change: the four states are driven by FIXTURE INPUTS, not by changing the loader. NAMED DEPENDENCY: a true 'corrupt-cache' state distinct from 'never-ran' requires the state loader to PRESERVE parse/load errors rather than collapse them into the missing-cache empty state; that loader/error-envelope change is called out as a dependency (handled as a bounded sub-step, or the live corrupt path is deferred until the loader preserves it — the Repair render still proves the state from fixture inputs).
steps: Build Repair's page on renderPage() + components: StatStrip, banded item list (each item a Card with its command as a CopyCommand), section headers per safety class
Relabel actions to honest 'Copy …' verbs; add copied + failed feedback; surface the fleet-vs-project scope + consequence next to the action
Render the four states (populated / empty / zero / corrupt) from FIXTURE INPUTS so the tab stays a render-layer change
Name the loader error-envelope dependency (preserve parse/load errors) in decisions; implement as a bounded sub-step or defer the live corrupt path

Repair journey test on producer state + fixture-driven render tests: assert items render (not just a count), labels say 'Copy', copied/failed feedback exists, and corrupt-vs-never-ran is distinguished from fixture inputs
features.acceptance: The Repair tab is rebuilt on the shared component layer: it lists the per-item repair set grouped by safety class (not just aggregate counts), every action is a copy-command with an honest 'Copy …' label + visible copied/failed feedback, and it distinguishes populated/empty/zero/corrupt states. Verified by a real-state→real-shell Repair journey test (producer state) PLUS fixture-driven render tests proving the corrupt-vs-never-ran distinction from fixture inputs; the loader error-envelope dependency is named in decisions and either implemented as a bounded sub-step or explicitly deferred.

features.description: Conformance checks that would have caught the audit's worst bug class, SCOPED so they do not contradict the six-tab deferral. Two checks: (a) emitted-class→CSS-rule resolution (catches the Repair / sr-* / cap-card-* / wn-gt-* / hlth-global-tools* unstyled-render failures); (b) token-only values (no raw hex/rgba/px font-size/px spacing). ENFORCEMENT IS TIERED. Blocking subset (fails the suite): the shared primitives (base + component CSS), the migrated Repair page, and the orphan-CSS guard. Advisory backlog: every other (unmigrated) tab is recorded in an explicit OFFENDER LEDGER; a test asserts the detector reports EXACTLY that current backlog WITHOUT failing the suite, so the debt is visible and shrinks as each tab migrates into the blocking subset. EXTRACTION MODEL: the detector is verified by synthetic pass/fail fixtures, and for migrated pages it reads the classes actually emitted from the REAL-SHELL DOM after journey boot (capturing dynamic / modifier / state classes), not by scraping static JS string literals.
steps: Implement the emitted-class→CSS-rule resolver: synthetic-fixture detector + real-shell-DOM extraction for migrated pages
Implement the token-only check; apply it (blocking) to base + component CSS + migrated Repair only
Add the explicit offender ledger for unmigrated tabs; a test asserts the detector reports exactly that backlog without failing the suite
Tests: a synthetic offender fails the blocking check; the migrated subset passes; the offender-ledger test matches the recorded backlog (and shrinks when a tab migrates)
features.acceptance: Two conformance checks exist — emitted-class→CSS-rule resolution and token-only values — enforced as BLOCKING for the shared primitives + the migrated Repair page + the orphan-CSS guard, and as an ADVISORY offender-ledger report for the unmigrated tabs (a test asserts the detector reports exactly the current backlog without failing the suite). The detector reads migrated-page classes from the real-shell DOM after journey boot and is itself verified by synthetic pass/fail fixtures. Verified by: the checks failing on a synthetic offender, passing on the migrated subset, and the offender-ledger test matching the recorded backlog.

features.description: Retire the 4 orphan pages. cloud-costs / command-center / financial / security are not in pageModules but index.html still loads their stylesheets, which redefine generic selectors (.activity-feed, .empty-state, .status-badge, .grid-2col, .token-meter) and silently restyle the 7 live pages via last-wins cascade (~1.8k dead-but-active lines). Remove their <link>s from index.html (and the page/lib files if dead), and add a guard that index.html loads CSS only for pages registered in pageModules.
steps: Remove the 4 orphan page CSS links from index.html; delete the orphan page/lib/css files if unreferenced
Add a test asserting index.html loads a stylesheet only for each page in the exported pageModules (no orphan CSS)
Re-run the full dashboard suite to confirm removing the orphan CSS did not rely on its bleed
features.acceptance: The 4 orphan pages' stylesheets are no longer loaded by index.html, and a test guards that index.html loads CSS only for pages in pageModules. Verified by that guard test passing and the full dashboard vitest suite remaining green after the orphan CSS is removed.
